subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Art of the One-on-One
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Art of the One-on-One.

hook.text: Andy Grove at Intel considered one-on-ones the most important tool in a manager's toolkit. Period.

buildup.text: A one-on-one is your dedicated time for alignment, feedback, and career conversation. Do not waste it on status.

discovery.text: Own the agenda. Bring topics that matter to you: blockers, career goals, feedback requests, or decisions needed.

twist.text: Most employees let their boss drive the one-on-one. The best employees drive it themselves and get more from it.

climax.text: Send a brief agenda 24 hours before. Include: what I need help with, what I accomplished, what I want to discuss.

punchline.text: Own your one-on-one. It's your career meeting.

quiz.question: Who should drive the one-on-one agenda?
options: The manager, since they are senior
The employee, since it is their career development time
HR should set a standard agenda for everyone
